title: NetFlow Settlement Codec Repair
scenario: A finance-ops team uses an internal Python service (~1,200 lines across 5 modules) that ingests raw NetFlow v9 records exported by routers, aggregates them into per-counterparty byte-transfer totals, and emits daily settlement files that feed a chargeback billing system. Since a recent refactor the nightly reconciliation job has started producing totals that drift from the router's own SNMP counters on certain traffic classes. No reproduction script was left; only the data files and service code are in the container. The environment contains a realistic set of NetFlow template records, data flowsets in binary files, and a reference totals CSV that the billing system trusts.
instruction_draft: Hey, our NetFlow settlement aggregator at /app is producing wrong per-counterparty byte totals for some traffic classes — the numbers don't match what the routers report via SNMP. Nobody left a repro. The rules are: (1) each data flowset record's byte count must be attributed to the counterparty identified by the source-IP-to-ASN mapping table, (2) when a flow template is re-exported mid-file the aggregator must use the most-recently-seen field layout for all subsequent records in that file, and (3) multi-file runs must carry template state forward across files in the order the files are processed (sorted by filename). Fix /app so that running `python /app/settle.py /app/data/` produces a `settlement.csv` whose per-counterparty totals match the reference computation for any valid set of NetFlow v9 binary input files.
requirements: Each data flowset record's byte count is attributed to the counterparty identified by the source-IP-to-ASN mapping table in /app/data/asn_map.csv.
When a flow template is re-exported mid-file, the aggregator uses the most-recently-seen field layout for all subsequent records in that file.
Multi-file runs carry template state forward across files processed in sorted filename order.
Running `python /app/settle.py /app/data/` produces a `settlement.csv` with correct per-counterparty byte totals.
environment: FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; pip install scapy==2.5.0 (for struct reference only, not used in app), no other unusual deps.
/app/settle.py — CLI entry point (~80 lines): discovers .bin files in the given directory, calls parser and aggregator, writes settlement.csv.

/app/netflow/parser.py (~300 lines): parses NetFlow v9 binary; BUG 1 — when a template flowset is re-encountered, the code skips updating the template cache ('if template_id in self.templates: continue') so it always uses the first-seen layout even after the router re-exports a revised template with a different field order.

/app/netflow/aggregator.py (~250 lines): accumulates per-ASN byte counts; BUG 2 — the aggregator creates a fresh parser (and therefore empty template cache) for each file rather than passing the persistent parser instance, so cross-file template state is lost.
/app/netflow/asn_lookup.py (~150 lines): CIDR-prefix trie for source-IP-to-ASN lookups; correct but plausibly suspicious.
/app/netflow/schema.py (~100 lines): NetFlow v9 field type constants; correct.
/app/data/asn_map.csv: 40 CIDR prefixes mapped to 8 ASN counterparty IDs.

/app/data/flows_001.bin through flows_006.bin: synthetically generated binary NetFlow v9 files; flows_003.bin re-exports a revised template mid-file; flows_004.bin through 006 depend on that revised template being carried forward.
/app/data/reference_totals.csv: ground-truth per-ASN byte totals computed by a reference implementation (used only inside the test suite, not shipped as a hint).

Test suite at /app/tests/test_settlement.py: generates fresh random NetFlow v9 binary inputs at verify time using a seeded reference encoder, runs settle.py, and compares output to reference totals computed inline.
internal_hint: There are exactly two bugs. BUG 1 is in parser.py: the guard `if template_id in self.templates: continue` must be removed (or changed to always overwrite) so that re-exported templates replace the cached layout. BUG 2 is in aggregator.py: a single Parser instance must be created once and reused across all files in sorted order rather than instantiated per file. Finding both requires reading parser.py carefully (the skip-on-duplicate logic is subtle), then noticing in aggregator.py that a new Parser() is constructed inside the per-file loop. The agent must trace a failing case through the binary files — flows_003.bin triggers BUG 1, and flows_004–006 trigger BUG 2 because they reference the template updated in 003. The reference totals CSV is not readable by the agent (it lives only inside the test); the agent must deduce correctness by reasoning about the spec and the code.
trap: An agent that only fixes BUG 1 (the template overwrite guard) will pass flows_003.bin in isolation but fail the cross-file tests because the aggregator still resets the parser per file. Conversely fixing only BUG 2 (sharing the parser) still fails because the first-seen template is never updated. The fuzz tests generate files where (a) a template is revised after initial export within a single file and (b) that revision is needed by a subsequent file; both conditions must hold simultaneously for the totals to match. Shallow testing against only the provided sample files (which happen to have flows_001–002 that need neither fix) will appear green.
tests: Smoke test: run settle.py on the provided /app/data/ directory and check that settlement.csv exists and has the expected ASN rows.

Fuzz test (N=40 input sets, seeded): generate random NetFlow v9 binary scenarios where each scenario includes: at least one mid-file template revision, at least two files where the second file references a template last seen in the first; compute reference totals with the reference encoder; run settle.py; assert per-ASN byte totals match within 0 bytes.

Cross-file ordering test: generate two files where file_b.bin's data records are only decodable with the template last exported in file_a.bin; verify settle.py produces correct totals only when files are processed in sorted (a before b) order.
Template overwrite test: generate a single file with the same template ID exported twice with different field orders; verify byte totals match the second (revised) layout.
Attribution test: generate flows with source IPs spanning multiple CIDR prefixes; verify bytes are attributed to the correct ASN counterparty, not aggregated under a catch-all.

verifier_knob.name: number_of_fuzz_scenarios
verifier_knob.effect: Raising to 80–120 increases the probability of hitting unusual template-revision patterns and multi-file orderings that expose partial fixes; lowering to 5–10 makes it easier for a partial fix to pass by luck.

expected_failure_modes: Agent fixes only the template-overwrite guard (BUG 1) and misses the per-file parser re-instantiation (BUG 2), passes the provided sample but fails cross-file fuzz tests.
Agent fixes only the per-file parser sharing (BUG 2) and misses the template-overwrite guard (BUG 1), fails fuzz scenarios with mid-file template revisions.
Agent reads asn_lookup.py or schema.py suspecting bugs there, spends time on the correct components, and runs out of time before tracing the real issues in parser.py and aggregator.py.
Agent rewrites the parser from scratch with correct logic but reintroduces the per-file instantiation pattern from the original aggregator.py structure.
Agent verifies only against the provided /app/data/ files (flows_001–002 don't exercise either bug) and concludes the code is already correct.
